package_info.why_malicious: This article is an industry overview and does not describe a specific malicious package or code. It discusses the growing risk of software supply chain attacks, referencing incidents like SolarWinds and CodeCov, and highlights the lack of detection and monitoring tools in most organizations. No specific malicious package or code is analyzed.

behavioral_signatures: Software tampering at any phase of the SDLC, such as unauthorized code changes in source repositories or build scripts.
Unauthorized modification of release packages or CI/CD artifacts, including insertion of malicious code or backdoors.
Unexpected changes in container images or build outputs, such as added files or altered binaries not present in source control.
file_indicators: Unexpected changes in build artifacts, such as mismatched checksums or unapproved files in release directories.
Modified or injected files in release packages, including files not present in the original source repository.
Altered container images, such as additional layers or binaries not accounted for in the build process.
network_indicators: Unusual outbound connections from build or CI/CD environments, especially to external or unapproved domains.
Connections to known malicious infrastructure during build or release, such as IPs or domains associated with previous supply chain attacks.
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Implement automated monitoring and integrity checks at every phase of the software development lifecycle (SDLC), including CI/CD pipelines, container builds, and release packaging. Use tools that can detect unauthorized changes, malware, backdoors, and exposed secrets in software artifacts before public distribution. Monitor for unexpected network activity from build environments and validate the integrity of all third-party and open-source dependencies using cryptographic signatures and checksums. Regularly audit build and deployment logs for anomalies.
